```{python}
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

output_dir = Path("data/processed/stage2_yz_distributions")
summary = pd.read_csv(output_dir / "distribution_summary.csv")
quintiles = pd.read_csv(output_dir / "forecast_error_quintiles.csv")
manifest = json.loads((output_dir / "distribution_manifest.json").read_text())


def markdown_table(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    columns = [str(column) for column in frame.columns]
    lines = [
        "| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |",
        "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in columns) + " |",
    ]
    for row in frame.itertuples(index=False):
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(str(value) for value in row) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)

labels = {
    "garch": "GARCH",
    "egarch": "EGARCH",
    "garch_x": "GARCH-X",
    "egarch_x": "EGARCH-X",
    "har_x": "HAR-X",
    "hgb": "HGB",
}
summary["model_label"] = summary["model"].map(labels)
order = list(labels)
summary["model"] = pd.Categorical(summary["model"], order, ordered=True)
summary = summary.sort_values(["model", "distribution"])

def paired(metric):
    wide = summary.pivot(index="model", columns="distribution", values=metric)
    wide["student_minus_normal"] = wide["student_t"] - wide["normal"]
    return wide

mae = paired("MAE")
log_score = paired("mean_negative_log_score")
n_common = int(summary["n_common"].iloc[0])
failures = int(summary["failure_count"].sum())
better_mae = int((mae["student_minus_normal"] < 0).sum())
better_score = int((log_score["student_minus_normal"] < 0).sum())

print("# Executive summary\n")
print(
    "This note compares one-step forecasts of unannualized two-observation "
    "Yang–Zhang volatility for LSEG Workspace GCc1. Six candidates are "
    f"re-estimated at each expanding origin from {manifest['test_start']} "
    f"through {manifest['test_end']}. Metrics below use the "
    f"{n_common} target dates on which every candidate and both "
    "distributions converged. "
    f"Recorded fit failures across all candidate-distribution rows: {failures}."
)
print()
print(
    f"Student-t lowers the level MAE for {better_mae} of 6 candidates and "
    f"lowers the mean negative log score for {better_score} of 6. "
    "These are descriptive scores on a holdout that earlier comparisons "
    "already used. They are not a test that one distribution forecasts better, "
    "and they do not select an operational model."
)
print()
print("# Specification\n")
print(
    "GARCH and EGARCH are AR(1) models from the `arch` package, fit by "
    "Normal or standardized Student-t maximum likelihood. GARCH-X uses the "
    "same AR(1) mean with a GARCH recursion in lagged OHLC range and the "
    "selected DXY, gold IV 1M, and gold IV 1Y predictors. Predictor "
    "coefficients in GARCH-X stay nonnegative. EGARCH-X puts those lagged "
    "inputs in a log-variance recursion. This GARCH-X Normal fit is the "
    "Gaussian special case of that likelihood, not the earlier threshold-GARCH variant."
)
print()
print(
    "HAR-X regresses log volatility on the HAR lags and the same origin-dated "
    "inputs. The Normal fit is least squares; the Student-t fit is maximum "
    "likelihood. HistGradientBoosting is unchanged squared-error boosting on "
    "log volatility, so its two point forecasts are identical. Its Normal and "
    "Student-t scales are estimated from residuals on a chronological "
    "training-only calibration slice."
)
print()
print(
    "Student-t innovations are scaled to unit variance and the degrees of "
    "freedom are estimated above 2. Log-volatility models report the "
    "conditional median, exp(log location), as the level forecast. Under a "
    "log Student-t innovation the conditional mean of the level need not be "
    "finite, so the median is the point forecast used for MAE, RMSE, and QLIKE. "
    "The negative log score is the predictive density of the volatility level. "
    "Log-volatility densities include the Jacobian."
)
print()
print("# Common-date performance\n")

display_columns = [
    "model_label",
    "distribution",
    "failure_count",
    "MAE",
    "RMSE",
    "QLIKE",
    "mean_negative_log_score",
    "coverage_90",
    "mean_width_90",
    "df_median",
]
table = summary[display_columns].copy()
table["coverage_90"] = table["coverage_90"].map(lambda value: f"{100 * value:.1f}%")
for column in ("MAE", "RMSE", "QLIKE", "mean_negative_log_score", "mean_width_90", "df_median"):
    table[column] = table[column].map(lambda value: "" if pd.isna(value) else f"{value:.6g}")
table = table.rename(columns={
    "model_label": "Model",
    "distribution": "Distribution",
    "failure_count": "Failures",
    "mean_negative_log_score": "Mean NLS",
    "coverage_90": "90% coverage",
    "mean_width_90": "Mean 90% width",
    "df_median": "Median df",
})
print(markdown_table(table))
print()
print(
    "QLIKE uses the squared forecast and squared outcome as variance proxies. "
    "A lower mean negative log score is a better density forecast. Interval "
    "coverage is the share of outcomes inside the model's 90% predictive "
    "interval. Width is the mean upper-minus-lower bound on the volatility level."
)
print()
print("# Forecast-level error dispersion\n")
print(
    "Earlier residual checks found that raw forecast-error variance rose with "
    "the forecast level. The table below reports that dispersion for the "
    "lowest and highest within-model forecast quintiles. A Student-t "
    "innovation can fatten predictive intervals without removing this "
    "conditional-variance pattern."
)
print()
edges = quintiles.loc[quintiles["forecast_quintile"].isin([1, 5])].copy()
edges["model_label"] = edges["model"].map(labels)
edges["model"] = pd.Categorical(edges["model"], order, ordered=True)
edges = edges.sort_values(["model", "distribution", "forecast_quintile"])
edge_table = edges[
    ["model_label", "distribution", "forecast_quintile", "n", "mean_forecast", "error_variance"]
].copy()
edge_table["mean_forecast"] = edge_table["mean_forecast"].map(lambda value: f"{value:.6g}")
edge_table["error_variance"] = edge_table["error_variance"].map(lambda value: f"{value:.6g}")
edge_table = edge_table.rename(columns={
    "model_label": "Model",
    "distribution": "Distribution",
    "forecast_quintile": "Quintile",
    "n": "N",
    "mean_forecast": "Mean forecast",
    "error_variance": "Error variance",
})
print(markdown_table(edge_table))
print()

def variance_ratio(model, distribution):
    block = quintiles.loc[
        quintiles["model"].eq(model) & quintiles["distribution"].eq(distribution)
    ]
    low_rows = block.loc[block["forecast_quintile"].eq(1), "error_variance"]
    high_rows = block.loc[block["forecast_quintile"].eq(5), "error_variance"]
    if low_rows.empty or high_rows.empty or float(low_rows.iloc[0]) <= 0:
        return None
    return float(high_rows.iloc[0]) / float(low_rows.iloc[0])

ratios = [
    variance_ratio(model, distribution)
    for model in order
    for distribution in ("normal", "student_t")
]
ratios = [ratio for ratio in ratios if ratio is not None]
above = sum(ratio > 1 for ratio in ratios)
print(
    f"For {above} of {len(ratios)} model-distribution pairs with both edge "
    "quintiles, the highest-quintile error variance exceeds the lowest. "
    f"The ratios run from {min(ratios):.2f} to {max(ratios):.2f}. "
    "A ratio above one means the larger forecasts still have more dispersed "
    "realized errors under that distribution."
)
print()
print("# Limits\n")
print(
    "Origins use only information available at the forecast origin, including "
    "the next-weekday availability proxy for DXY and the two gold implied "
    "volatilities. Adjacent Yang–Zhang targets overlap, so forecast errors are "
    "dependent and the common-date scores are not independent replications. "
    "No paired forecast-loss test or untouched later holdout is reported. "
    "Optimizer convergence does not imply a unique global maximum. "
    f"Training length at the first origin is {int(manifest['training_observations'])} "
    "valid targets."
)
```
